observed_evidence: Preliminary ship-tracking data reported by Reuters showed 10 commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz on September 23, up from 7 the prior day but below the roughly 17-vessel 10-day moving average and far below the roughly 125 large commercial vessels per day before the February 28 war.
Reuters reported U.S.-Iran diplomacy continued without concrete progress; Iran continued to prioritize lifting the U.S. naval blockade and reopening Hormuz in its proposals.
At 09:40 GMT on September 24, Reuters reported Brent futures at $105.51/bbl and WTI at $93.90/bbl; these are intraday observations, not settlements.
semantic_interpretation: Visible Hormuz traffic improved from the prior day but remains severely impaired versus both the recent moving average and pre-war normal. Active diplomacy provides de-escalation optionality, but the lack of concrete progress and renewed oil-price risk premium keep energy-inflation, freight and Taiwan input-cost risks elevated. The visible-vessel count may understate actual flows because AIS-dark transits are not captured.
fair_value_policy: Fair Value V2.1 remains the sole valuation baseline; this event does not calculate or modify Fair Value.
